title: Route Conductor: Visual Policy Builder for Region-aware Tiering & Model Fallbacks
creator: Ariela Morgan
description:
Goal: Ship a Console-first visual policy editor (Route Conductor) that lets customers author, validate, and preview region-aware tier routing and fallback model variants without writing DSLs. The editor should make safe choices the default, expose explicit fallbacks and region constraints, and provide a dry-run preview with cost/latency and SLA impact estimates.

Problem statement: Customers need a single place to express routing preferences (region affinity, tier prioritization, and fallback model variants) that maps to runtime routing behavior (smart routing engine). Today, policies are either delivered as text DSLs or buried in engineer-only configs; customers want an intuitive, auditable UI with safety checks and lightweight simulation.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement backend scheduling optimizations, autoscaler changes, or private deployment install flows — those are separate engineering sub-issues. It focuses on the Console editor, validation rules, and preview runner integration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Visual editor supports: region selectors (include/exclude), ordered tier routing (primary, secondary, fallback), and fallback chains of model variants with per-variant weight/threshold controls.
- Editor exposes explicit compatibility hints (e.g., tokenizer/runtime compatibility) and flags incompatible selections with actionable fixes.
- Validation engine runs lint-style checks and surface severity (error/warning/info) inline. Blocking errors must prevent save/deploy.
- Dry-run preview executes against a synthetic trace and shows: expected latency distribution, estimated per-token cost delta, probability of hitting fallback (based on capacity heuristics), and sample output differences (when variant outputs are available).
- UX contains a lightweight audit trail of edits (who changed what) and an easy rollback to last known-good policy.
- End-to-end tests and a representative acceptance harness exist and are checked into the repo (links below).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Visual blocks vs DSL: We will prioritize a block-based composer (drag-to-order tiers + modal for model variant details). We will keep an "advanced DSL" view read-only to show the underlying rule language to experts but make edits via the visual UI first. This minimizes errors and keeps the product approachable.
- Failure modes: Default policy templates will include a safe fallthrough model (low-cost, small-context variant) to prevent total outage. Customers can opt-out but must explicitly acknowledge increased risk.
- Suggestion engine: The editor will recommend region-first routing when request geo aligns with capacity regions and will surface a cost/latency tradeoff panel. Recommendation logic is heuristic-driven initially and will be replaced by telemetry-driven suggestions later.
- Preview fidelity: Preview uses sampled telemetry and a lightweight capacity model to estimate fallback probability; it is intentionally conservative and marked as "simulation".

Telemetry & metrics to track on rollout:
- % of customers using visual editor vs DSL
- Rate of validation errors per policy save
- Preview-adjusted policies that reduced fallback rate in production
- Time-to-first-successful-deploy from editor

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal beta with solutions engineers and 3 pilot customers (2 weeks). Validate UX and telemetry.
2) Beta: opt-in for all customers with feature flag; collect telemetry and iterate (4 weeks).
3) GA: enable by default for new workspaces with clear opt-out + migration docs (2 weeks).

Notes for Eng handoff:
- Provide schema: policy -> {regionSelectors, tierList[], fallbackChain[]} (see confluence link). Editor will POST policies to /api/v1/policies and call /api/v1/policies/validate (sync) and /api/v1/policies/preview (async).
- Preview runner will accept a small sample payload set and return metrics. For speed, previews are rate-limited and cached per-policy-hash.

Open questions:
- Should the editor surface live capacity signals (real-time) or only historical heuristics? Initial scope: heuristics only; follow-up to add live signal integration.
- How strict should compatibility checks be across private deployments with restricted model sets? Proposal: make checks conservative and offer a toggle for permissive mode behind admin-only flag.

Links to artifacts and prototypes are below in attachments.
